🇮🇱 ⚠️ #Netanyahu Claims #Arab Parties Stole #Israel's Election, Demands Investigation After Arab Voter Gains, No Majority Deadlocked Results: 
Washington Examiner: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday said rival Arab parties cheated in his country’s elections after exit polls indicated his coalition failed to capture a majority in the #Knesset, pushing the Middle Eastern democracy into a political deadlock.
Netanyahu’s Likud party and its allies outperformed expectations on Tuesday. But with results still trickling in on Wednesday evening, the prime minister failed to keep his majority in the Israeli parliament. There is still no clear winner. The opposition bloc, led by Gadi #Eisenkot’s Yashar party, remains Likud’s top rival. But two Arab parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, outperformed as they gained seats, drawing historic support as they are to win their largest-ever share of the vote.
Before the election, Netanyahu’s coalition held around 68 of the 120 Knesset seats, and the main opposition to him held around 49 seats.
With roughly 89% of the vote counted Wednesday evening, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats. The main opposition, led by Eisenkot’s Yashar bloc, held 48 seats.
No bloc reached the winning number of 61 lawmakers, the size of a Knesset coalition necessary to form a government. But Arab parties made the biggest gains, with 19 seats, up from the 10 held by the United Arab List and the Joint List before the elections.
Netanyahu said the Arab parties had stolen the election, claiming they are guilty of criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters.
“This is a serious blow to Israeli democracy and the voting rights of Israeli citizens,” he said in a post to X. “The law enforcement agencies must act with an iron fist and in an immediate manner.”
Netanyahu demanded election authorities in Israel immediately investigate his allegations, promising that his Likud party would produce hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence regarding election theft in many Arab polling stations, including thousands of envelopes with cash and Ra’am slips, threats and violence against polling station members, multiple voting behind the curtain, voting with double identities, discrepancies between the number of envelopes and the number of voters, and the use of prohibited mobilization software."

events.text:
🇺🇸 US faces uphill battle in the drone production race
The US is starting “basically from zero” in mass-producing cheap military drones, Bloomberg cites a senior Pentagon official as admitting, exposing the scale of its struggle to catch up with Russia and China. 
While its rivals can manufacture millions of expendable UAVs, the US is still trying to build the factories, supply chains and procurement systems needed to produce them at scale. The Pentagon has poured roughly $1.1 billion into its Drone Dominance program, a four-stage contest designed to push manufacturers through increasingly demanding tests and larger orders to prove they can mass-produce drones.
American manufacturers face three major obstacles:
🌏 China dominates production of key components, including batteries, brushless motors, propellers and cameras; US manufacturers must find alternative suppliers to comply with restrictions on Chinese parts, often paying significantly more for components
🌏 drone technology and countermeasures evolve within weeks - manufacturers must continuously update software and hardware while simultaneously scaling production
🌏 the US military's procurement system is built around expensive, complex weapons developed over years, not disposable drones that must be produced cheaply and replaced in huge numbers
A previous Biden-era initiative, Replicator, promised a swarm of attack drones, yet fell far short of its target, delivering only several hundred drones against a goal of thousands. Meanwhile, China could rapidly scale production to 500,000 drones a month, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.
The Pentagon's proposed budget allocates $55 billion to autonomous warfare, including $17 billion for drones and other uncrewed systems. But the funding push could face political headwinds after the midterms if Democrats take control of Congress.
